Possibility and Uncertainty in the Past
There are a variety of ways to express uncertainty and to talk about possibility about past times.
Look at the chart for a summary of what modals you can use and how to use them:
We couldn't have had better timing.
We should have gotten here sooner, but Vanessa was slow.
I couldn't have ran any faster.
The weather report could have told us there was going to be a blizzard.
I would have carried you, but chivalry is dead.

The Past Continuous vs. The Simple Past
When you want to talk about two events that happened at the same time in the past, you can use either the Simple Past or the Past Continuous tenses.

For example:
Max was watching TV while Beth was making dinner.
Max watched TV while Beth made dinner.

When you choose to use the Past Continuous, you are focusing the fact that the event or action was in progress in the past.
When you choose to use the Simple Past, you are focusing on the fact that the event or action was completed.

When you talk about two past completed events, you use the Simple Past for both.

For example:
He got up after the alarm went off.
Initially, she was living in Austria and she was skiing everyday while working in a ski resort near Innsbruck.
Next, she was planning a trip to Italy.
But then cancelled that and went to Croatia instead.
But after that,  I read on her blog that she was traveling to Bratislava because she wanted to go to Moscow after.
I was taking a shower when the phone rang.
By the time I picked it up, the person had hung up.

images.text:
Amy: Wow, we couldn't have had better timing.
Peter: We should have gotten here sooner, but Vanessa slowed us down.
Vanessa: Brrr. I'm sorry. I couldn't have run any faster. I wore the wrong shoes. I thought we were going out on the town not snowshoeing. You should have carried me, Peter.

Peter: Oh, I would have carried you, but chivalry is dead. Oww!
Amy: Hi, table for three.
Vanessa: The weather report could have told us there was going to be a blizzard. I didn't hear anything about it.
Amy: I think It's beautiful. Excuse me, I need to go to the washroom.
Peter: So what were you doing when I called last night? I got your machine.

Vanessa: I was writing an e-mail to Sally when you called. Sorry. I didn't feel like answering.
Peter: Oh, so what is Sally up to these days?
Vanessa: Well this month, initially, she was living in Austria and she was skiing everyday while working in a ski resort near Innsbruck. Next, she was planning a trip to Italy, but then canceled that and went to Croatia instead.
Peter: Yeah. But after that, I read on her blog that she was traveling to Bratislava because she wanted to go to Moscow after. That was a week ago. She wants to ride the Trans-Siberian railway remember.
Vanessa: Right. I forgot about that. Yeah, so now she must be in Moscow. I think she called the other day. I was taking a shower when the phone rang. By the time I picked it up, the person had hung up. The call display showed a Russian number. It was probably her. I hope she is okay.
Peter: You know Sally, she always lands on her feet.
Amy: What did I miss?
Peter: Nothing. Let's have some coffee.
